small_guidance:
- The GEMM is 128×16384×16384 — M=128 is tiny. Drop BLOCK_M to 32 or 64 in all autotune configs and increase BLOCK_N to 256 with BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3-4 to maximize N-tile parallelism and K-pipeline depth. Configs with BLOCK_M=128 waste compute since only 128 rows exist total.
- Enable GROUP_M swizzle properly: with M=128 and BLOCK_M=32, there are only 4 row tiles; set GROUP_M=4 (or keep 1) but make sure the autotune list explores GROUP_M∈{1,4,8} for L2 reuse across N tiles.
- Softmax over N=16384 with BLOCK_N=16384 requires 64KB/row in registers — try a two-pass (online) softmax kernel with BLOCK_N=2048 or 4096 and num_warps=8 to reduce register pressure and spills; the current single-pass resident kernel likely spills heavily.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a split-K / streamK GEMM since K=16384 is the dominant dimension and M=128 leaves the grid under-occupied (only ~64 tiles at BLOCK_N=256). A split-K kernel with atomic-add accumulation, or a persistent streamK schedule, will fill the 128 SMs of the 4090 far better than the current data-parallel tiling.
- Fuse the softmax into the GEMM epilogue using an online (Welford-style) max/sum across N-tiles: after split-K reduction per row tile, run a second small kernel (or a persistent reducer) that computes row max and sum in a single pass over the materialized GEMM output, avoiding the BLOCK_N=16384 register-resident softmax.
- Consider running the matmul in tf32 (`tl.dot(..., allow_tf32=True)` / input cast) since inputs are fp32 on Ampere/Ada — tf32 tensor cores give ~2× throughput vs. fp32 emulation and still pass the 5e-2 tolerance.
